elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 27.2: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York." This replaces the former no-choice-of-law provision that directed all facts pointing to a national law be disregarded.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Rendered 27.2: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute ... provided that any Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief, so the merits forum remains exclusive; the conforming edit to 27.1 removed the prior "determine the method, such as arbitration" and "sole and exclusive remedy" language that would otherwise have displaced the court forum.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered 27.2 selects the laws of the State of New York, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not a defect: the preferred level is complete, and the fallback is offered in the margin comment only as an alternative.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Rendered 27.2 designates the state and federal courts in New York County, consistent with the preferred (not fallback) forum. Not a defect given preferred completion.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: both preferred elements are satisfied in operative language — New York governing law plus exclusive New York County state and federal court jurisdiction over the merits with only a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out (a customary carve-out that preserves exclusivity of the merits forum).

The clause was correctly scoped as a deviation approaching walk-away territory: original 27.2 contained no choice of law and affirmatively excluded the facts needed to identify one, and original 27.1 made Management Committee referral — expressly including a committee-imposed arbitration, potentially seated abroad — the "sole and exclusive remedy," leaving no court forum.

Minimal: the substituted 27.2 replaces only the choice-of-law/forum provision, and the 27.1 edit is confined to what was necessary to remove the two contradictory mechanics (committee power to "determine the method, such as arbitration" and the "sole and exclusive remedy" sentence) that would otherwise have overridden the new exclusive court forum. No survival tails, expense allocation, procedures, or other extras were added.

Preserves intent: the good-faith resolution effort, the Management Committee escalation step, and the "performance shall continue during the resolution of any dispute" sentence are all retained; the new cross-reference from 27.1 to Paragraph 27.2 resolves cleanly and leaves no undefined term or dangling reference.

No further repair is required. Note for the negotiation record only (not a defect): the fallback laws/fora (Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London) are offered in the margin comment and would remain acceptable if Vendor resists New York.
